messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: More Dynamic UI, creating selecInput without <htmlOutput> in ui.R
parts:
I do not think performance is the primary reason. eval(parse()) just
looks so bad and unnecessary. What input$foo does is to turn the
symbol foo into a character string "foo", and extract the element
named "foo" in input. Then it is just so straightforward to make the
character name in the very beginning and use input[["foo"]] directly.

The $ method also has a few limitations, due to the R syntax
requirement, e.g. normally you cannot have spaces in the symbol name,
so you cannot do input$foo bar (have to input$`foo bar`), or you
cannot do input$in since 'in' is a reserved keyword. Weird things like
this can happen, but [[]] will always work, e.g. input[["foo bar"]],
input[["in"]], ... Note this is not specific to Shiny. It is a general
issue in R.

In other cases, eval(parse()) is often an indication of the awkward
design of the program. Normally you do not have to write code that
generates code. That said, I myself use eval(parse()) a lot for other
purposes :)

Regards,
Yihui
--

Since "input" is a list and returnes NULL for empty adresses I wrote a function

    input.vector                <- function(name, number) {
       
           parse(text = paste("c(", paste(name,number,sep="",collapse=","), ")",sep=""))
    }

which you can use like  this:

   eval(input.vector("input$a",1:100))

if you for example to not generate more than 100 dynamical input elements of the same kind.

messages.subject: Re: More Dynamic UI, creating selecInput without <htmlOutput> in ui.R
parts:
Never use eval(parse(input$a)) in a Shiny app, or anything that looks like that.

The reason is not elegance, it's security. What happens if the (malicious) user decides to set input$a to system("rm -rf ~/")?

The only time it is remotely OK to use eval(parse()) in Shiny is if you can guarantee that the value you're evaluating could not possibly have come from user input (that includes from a database whose values came from the user).

I am also working on a similar UI where user can dynamically add controls on the fly (renderUI). I am able to add controls dynamically but not able to retain their input values if the user has already selected values before pressing the 'add' button. 

Here is my code:
 

ui.R

library(shiny)
shinyUI(navbarPage(inverse=TRUE,title = "BA Database",
                   tabPanel("Home",uiOutput("dynButtons"))
))

server.R

library(shiny)
library(shinysky)

shinyServer(function(input,output, session){

    basicItems <- function(x){fluidRow(
        tags$head(tags$style(type="text/css", "select { width: 125px;}")),
        column(1,selectInput(paste0("alpha",x),"",c("table","a","b","c"))),
        column(1,offset=1,selectInput(paste0("beta",x),"",c("variable","1","2","3")))
    )}

    i=1
    items <- basicItems(i)

    output$dynButtons <- renderUI({
        uiOutput("genControls")
    })
    

        output$genControls <- renderUI({
            fluidPage(
                fluidRow(
                    column(2,offset=10,actionButton("addButton","Add~!"))
                ),
                fluidRow(
                    column(12,getItems())
                )
            )
        })
    

    addItems <- reactive({
            n_click <- input$addButton

            if(is.null(n_click)) {
                items <- basicItems(i); 
                return()}
            if(n_click > 0){
                    i = i+1;
                    items <<- list(items,basicItems(i))    
            }
            return()
    })    
    
    getItems <- reactive({
        addItems()
        return(items)
    })
    
})
